rulings: Q1 ANSWERED — the sheet ABSORBS the popover, it does not compete with it. "Click on your own tower, you can see the character sheet with the fix scrape as today... You are just adding those two options to there." One panel; it simply looks different when the thing is yours. Enemy buildings get the sheet with no FIX/SCRAP.
Q2 ANSWERED — no skills, no abilities. "The six boss skills, you should not add for now. Let us keep them out of the character sheets."
Q3 ANSWERED — buildings DO get a sheet, because you want to see how much health they have. NOT creature-only.

NEW, he designed it himself — a building that creates ONE creature (Helga hub, the Voltkin TV) shows the BUILDING health, and underneath it a little image of the character it owns plus that character health. Clicking that little image opens the character own sheet; so does clicking the character on the board.

LAYOUT FIX — the derived number must sit on the row it derives FROM. "150 a swing is right where the attack row is, so the 260 pool should be where the HP row is." My draft had the pool on the DEF row.

PORTRAIT — use the generated art we already have: a plain idle frame, zoomed in on the face. A thing WITH tower art uses how the tower looks. A thing with NO art yet uses the codex look — the shape-and-connector emblem.

scope_amendments.title: TARGETING — his rulings. Priority 2 is now specified, still NOT started.
rulings: Q1 ANSWERED — OPTION A, and he widened what "building" means: "the closest thing that has connectors... the closest shapes that are connected to something else. It doesn't have to be like an actual building. Any structure." So the target is ANY connected component, not only a recipe-complete tower.

OPTION B IS DEAD BY HIS OWN LOGIC — "nothing attacks [shapes]. So B can't even be. You can't attack a shape if it's connected. You're attacking the connectors. You only attack a shape when there's no connectors left, when it's the lone shape left on the map." The S179 rule stands exactly as shipped.

SUICIDE GOBLIN — buildings first. BUT: "if there's any units on his way to the building and he's below like 50% health, then he's gonna look for anything that's close." A health-gated switch to nearest-anything.
PENCIL CHEWER — "only buildings and connectors. They do NOT attack people no matter what. If there's no buildings, then they don't attack." NEVER people, under any condition.

LASER TURRET — HE CHANGED R72. "Maybe it doesn't do both. It does only creatures, so that's fine." The DECLARED table is what is wrong, not the beam. Fix DEFENDER_TARGETS.turret BOTH -> UNITS_ONLY. No behaviour change.
STINK TOWER creatures only · HELGA units only · CASTLE GUN creatures only — all three ACCEPTED as shipped.

VOLTKIN own-connector fallback is INTENDED but narrower than shipped: "when there's no enemy units or enemy buildings — when only the castle of the enemy is left, yes, he goes on your own connectors." Today it falls back whenever no enemy BOND exists, without checking enemy units.

"PREFER UNITS" IS PER-UNIT, NOT GLOBAL — "depends on if it's a creature that only attacks a specific unit, kind of like pencil chewers, or just a creature that has preferences, like a bomber." Specialists vs preference-havers.
HE SAID THE TABLE IS INCOMPLETE — "I feel like we did not run through everything. Who targets what? I feel like it's not 100% correct." Completing it outranks starting the code.
AND HE COULD NOT PARSE "21 of 24 unit types" — "What the fuck does that mean?" Speak in what he SEES. That is the S179 muscle-memory rule, broken again.

reflexion_entries_to_archive: A BLIND RENDERER LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE MISSING LOGIC. Three of his six defects were data the model already computed and the card never read - actions (FIX/SCRAP/FEED), the portrait art, the race colour. Before building anything for a "missing" feature, grep whether the VIEW already carries it. heightFor reserving no space is why nothing even looked clipped.

DERIVE THE LITERAL FROM THE CONSTANT OR THE RE-PIN HAPPENS A THIRD TIME. The +42px stat column, the toBe(8) shot and the toBe(1015) regen all went red on an owner retune. Each is now expressed as the arithmetic under test (statValueColumnPx, attackFifths(CASTLE_ATK, CASTLE_PEN), 1000 + rate), so the next retune re-pins itself. Keep ONE literal as a deliberate tripwire on an OWNER NUMBER (CASTLE_MAX_HP) so a human is forced to re-read the ruling.

AN OWNER NUMBER GIVEN IN PERCENT IS NOT THE SAME AS ITS CONSEQUENCE. R128 was 1.0-1.8% of max; 15/18/21/24/27 was only what that meant at a 1500 pool. Raising the pool legitimately raised regen to 25/30/35/40/45, and pinning the old absolutes would have OVERRIDDEN his ruling while looking like honouring it. Surface the derived buff to him instead of choosing for him.

RE-MEASURE, NEVER REASON, WHEN TWO CHANGES PULL OPPOSITE WAYS. Pool x1.67 and gun x5 landed together; the siege threshold moved only ~1.2x (8..10 -> 10..12), not the 1.67x the pool implies, because the stronger gun thins the push. A temporary probe through the real host tick gave the true table in one run.

A TEST THAT PREDICTS ITS OWN FAILURE IS THE CHEAPEST GUARD THERE IS. castleRegen.test.ts said "if CASTLE_MAX_HP ever moves, this case is the one that should go red first." It was, and it forced a human to re-read R128 instead of the buff shipping silently. Write that sentence when a value is derived.

DOCK, DO NOT DUPLICATE, WHEN MERGING TWO INTERACTIVE SURFACES.
